# Tips

The Tip of the Day collection (Help > Tip of the Day...), all on one page.

**The image canvas.** Your layers are drawn on the canvas. Scroll to zoom, drag to rotate or pan (the Rotate and Pan buttons on the toolbar choose which), and double-click to reset the view.

**Add data.** New Layer adds data for the time range and time step beside it. Pick a format at the top of its menu: JPEG 2000 for fast Helioviewer images, FITS (VSO) for calibrated files, or FITS (native) for a mission's own archive.

**Drop files in.** Drop FITS or JPEG 2000 files anywhere on the window to load them as image layers; drop a .jhv file to open that session.

**Nothing loaded yet?.** Help > Open Demo Scene opens a new session with a bundled SDO/AIA 171 image and RHEF on; nothing to download.

**Colour and brightness.** Select a layer in the list to see its options. Under Display, Color picks the color table; under Intensity, the two Levels handles set the brightness window.

**Play the movie.** Play runs the movie and the arrows beside it step one frame at a time. J, K and L play backward, stop and play forward from anywhere in the window.

**Find any control.** Help > Search Controls... finds any command or control by name and shows you where it is: Cmd-K on a Mac, Ctrl-K elsewhere.

**Ask a control.** Rest the pointer on any button, box or slider for a moment and a tooltip says what it does.

**Take the tour.** Help > Tours > Getting started steps through the main controls, one at a time; Help > Tours lists the other tours.

**More tours.** Help > Tours has short guided tours: loading data, making a movie, views and projections, and sharing your work.

**Your own starting scene.** File > Set Current Session as Default opens this scene at every start, ahead of the last session.

**Present.** View > Present shows the output only, full screen. Esc leaves.

**Where did this come from?.** File > Copy Provenance puts the program, its build and each layer's data source on the clipboard.

**Undo.** Edit > Undo takes back the last change to the scene.

**Reading an RHEF image.** RHEF, in a layer's Filter list, is a visualization, not a calibrated radiance. Measure on the original data, with the filter set to None.

**Fewer frames, faster.** Time step, beside New Layer, sets the time between frames for the next layer; tick Frame count to set how many frames instead. The line under it estimates the video length before anything downloads.

**Change a layer's data.** Double-click a layer's name in the layer list to change its dataset.

**The newest PUNCH day.** Layers > PUNCH Latest opens the newest day of PUNCH clear average mosaics (CAM) in Helioradial with RHEF.

**Before and after.** Layers > Duplicate Layer adds a copy of the selected image layer. Compare, on the toolbar, then blinks between two layers or swipes a divider across the view.

**Every channel at once.** Pizza, on the toolbar, cuts every shown image layer into its own wedges of one Sun, so the same patch is seen through every filter. Turn the cut, or record a seamless spin while the data stands still.

**Side by side.** Multiview, on the toolbar, puts each shown image layer in a view of its own, side by side.

**Change the projection.** Projection, on the toolbar, opens a palette that changes how the Sun is mapped onto the screen: Orthographic, HPC, Helioradial or Latitudinal.

**Timelines.** The Timelines pane plots time series and events against the movie time. Click an empty part of the plot to move the movie to that time.

**Record a movie.** The red dot records the view as a movie; click it again to stop. Files go to the Exports folder inside the HFStudio folder in your home folder.

**A movie in one click.** File > Quick Share records one loop as a movie that plays anywhere, then shows it in the file manager; your recording settings are not changed.

**Trim the movie.** Movie > Trim Start Here (I) and Trim End Here (O) set the movie's in and out points at the current frame; Movie > Reset Trim clears them.

**Copy the picture.** Edit > Copy Frame puts the canvas picture on the clipboard, as an 8-bit screenshot.

**Send a scene to someone.** File > Share Scene... saves the scene for someone else, with your home folder written as ~ and any local files outside the cache listed first.

**Take it to another computer.** File > Export Session with Data... saves the session plus a .data.zip of its local files, to open on another computer.

**On to Python.** Layers > Send to Python writes the active layer's FITS files as double-precision science FITS, plus a manifest and a sunpy snippet.

**HDR.** HDR, on the toolbar, sets how the whole view is mapped into the display's extended range: headroom, mapping, knee, in-range share and clipped pixels.

**Tell the developer.** Help > Send Feedback... sends a problem, a request or a question to the developer; no account needed.

**Fewer tips.** Snooze, in this window, stops tips at startup for a day, a week or a month, and Show a tip at startup turns them off. Neither touches the Welcome window.

**One scene, many pictures.** Window > Study Manager... (File > Study Manager... off macOS) makes a set of pictures of one scene, each with its own projection, lambda, field of view or layers. Start from a template such as the lambda ladder, then Export set writes every picture, a manifest and the command that remakes them.

**What is still running.** The spinner at the bottom left turns while anything downloads, loads or computes, and becomes a check when everything has landed. Click it for the Task Manager: the running work, anything that did not land, and the export queue.
